items.text: **Changed: the remote's own controls are three small icons in a column down its left side, inside the frame** (pin, move, close), the way Dimitry sketched it, instead of floating above it. Quiet grey; they turn yellow only when on.

**Fixed: a sound on a roaming path could not be moved to another shape.** Dragging it onto a shape made a small marker appear there, but the sound went back to roaming, because its path kept pulling it home. A sound now leaves its path when you drop it on a shape and stays on that shape's vertex. Pressing and then dragging also no longer leaves a ghost of the sound behind.

**Changed: the remote's own controls (move, pin, close) are one quiet strip on its top edge,** outside the tiles, plain grey glyphs like a heads-up display's pin and arrows. They turn yellow only when they are on (pinned, or being moved). The close tile is gone from the grid.

**Fixed: moving paths left behind as ghosts.** When a sound with a wandering or recorded path was taken away, swapped or let go while its ring was open, the old path kept playing as a ghost with no sound to belong to, and nothing could remove it. Ghosts with no sound are now cleared away on their own.

**Changed: the remote's move and pin handles sit on its corners, outside the tiles.** Two round gold handles (move at the top left, pin at the top right) make it clear they act on the remote itself, not on the thing you are editing.

**Fixed: a sound dragged onto another shape slid back to where it came from.** After you let go, the sound was pulled back to its old vertex before the field could notice where you dropped it, so it only joined the new shape when the timing happened to be kind. It now joins the moment you let go, and the catching distance is twice as wide. The shape can be any shape on the field, not only the main drawing; a gold line shows which one will take it while you drag.

**New: the remote can be pulled away and pinned.** The remote (the bar of tiles beside the object you touched) has two new tiles: *move* (drag it anywhere in the field; a dotted line stays tied to the object; it snaps to an edge or corner when you let go) and *pin* (it stays there whatever object you touch, and comes back there the next time, even after you close the app).

**Fixed: the remote no longer chases a moving object.** It used to follow a moving handle and hop from side to side. It now sits beside the object once and holds still, and only glides out of the way if the object drifts into it.

**Changed: a locked row or column is now cool grey-blue, not yellow.** Locked lines (the padlock at the edge turns gold) were tinted the same yellow-brown as a play line, so they looked like play lines that had frozen. To clear one, tap its padlock at the edge of the grid.

**Fixed: on a wide screen (about 1500 px and up) the tempo bar sat on top of undo and redo.** The tempo bar was floated over the row to centre it; it now sits in the row between the other buttons and takes the room that is left.

**Fixed: choosing a line-up did nothing with a mouse, trackpad or pen.** In the robot's line-up menu (Orbit, Cross, Four winds and the rest), the list grabbed the pointer, so the click never reached the button you pressed. A finger worked, which hid it. Every pointer works now.

**Tempo now comes back down.** Raising the tempo quickly and then setting it back to 20 left the music (and held notes) running fast, because the slow glide to the new tempo took its wobble from wherever the glide had got to. The wobble is now fixed once per pass, so the tempo always lands on the slider.

**Redo no longer meets the tempo bar.** On an iPad in landscape at about 900 to 1000 px the tempo bar was squeezed until its speaker, metronome and slider piled up beside undo and redo. It now keeps a minimum width and the bar wraps to a second line when there is not room.
